question: Who among the following married the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and received the title 'Nur Jahan'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrunnisa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mehrunnisa**, later known as **Nur Jahan**, married Emperor Jahangir in 1611 and became his twentieth and most beloved wife.
 
• Nur Jahan, meaning "Light of the World," was a title conferred upon Mehrunnisa by Jahangir after their marriage.
 
• She became an influential figure in the Mughal court, wielding significant political power and even issuing royal orders (farmans) under her own name.
 
• Mehrunnisa was the daughter of Mirza Ghiyas Beg, a Persian noble, and she played a critical role in the cultural and administrative developments of the Mughal Empire.
 
• Her marriage to Jahangir marked her rise as one of the most powerful women in Mughal history, deeply involved in state affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nur Jahan's Political Influence:**

 
 
• She was actively involved in governance and is known to have participated in the imperial administration alongside Jahangir.
 
• Her name was inscribed on coins, a significant marker of her authority and influence.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to Mughal Art and Culture:**
 
 
• Nur Jahan was a patron of architecture, poetry, and the arts, commissioning several gardens and monuments.
 
• One of her most famous contributions was the design of the Itimad-ud-Daulah's Tomb in Agra, often referred to as the "Baby Taj."
 
 
 
• **Background of Mehrunnisa:**
 
 
• Mehrunnisa was born in 1577 in Kandahar, present-day Afghanistan, and her family migrated to India seeking fortune in the Mughal court.
 
• Before marrying Jahangir, she was previously married to Sher Afghan, a Mughal officer, who died under disputed circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Nur Jahan remains one of the most iconic and influential women in Mughal history, symbolizing power and elegance.
 
• Her life and achievements continue to inspire historical and literary works, showcasing her as a strong figure in a predominantly male-dominated era.
